parsed.rationale: The structural evidence explicitly reports `shared_field_count: 0` and `jaccard: null`, meaning the pipeline found no overlapping members between `AudioEnginePlayerProtocol` and `PlaybackController`. The surface-level resemblance is limited to a handful of method names (`installRenderTap`, `removeRenderTap`, `isPlaying`, `play`, `stop`) but their signatures diverge materially: `PlaybackController.play` takes a `PlaybackReason` parameter and `stop` also takes `PlaybackReason`, while `AudioEnginePlayerProtocol.play` is parameterless and `stop` is parameterless; `AudioEnginePlayerProtocol` additionally owns `eventStream`, `scheduleBuffer`, `scheduleBuffers`, `volume`, and `makeRenderTapStream` — low-level audio-engine concerns absent from `PlaybackController`. The two protocols operate at different abstraction layers (raw AVAudio engine vs. higher-level playback orchestration), so introducing a shared parent protocol would either be vacuously thin or would incorrectly couple engine-level contracts to controller-level semantics.
